sections.h2: What can the Williamston registrar's office do for me?
sections.html:
It sits on the first floor of the Martin County Governmental Building in Williamston and keeps land records that its own page says reach back to 1771. Deeds, easements, agreements, deeds of trust, assignments, releases and plats all get recorded there, and the office maintains indexes for each, including one for plats.

Uniform commercial code filings that touch real estate are recorded in the same books as land documents, which the county dates to July 1, 2001. The office also records military discharge papers (DD-214), keeps assumed business name, partnership and incorporation filings, swears in notaries and indexes them, and lists the vital records it holds: births and deaths from October 1913 and marriage licenses from 1883, with an older marriage index from 1872 to 1882.

For a seller, one practical fact stands out. Anything the office has in its books is something a title searcher will find, so it is worth looking before the buyer does.

sections.h2: Is there a way to look through Martin County deeds from home?
sections.html:
Yes. Deeds can be viewed at martinrod.org, according to the county, and the images there reach back to 1771. Vital records can be ordered through a separate online service the page links, and a vital records index is online too.

An hour with the index is time well spent on an inherited or long-held house.

  • Search the owner's name and the name of whoever you inherited from.
  • Compare the legal description on the last deed with the tax record.
  • Look for deeds of trust that have no release recorded after them.
  • Note any plat or state right of way plan that touches the lot.

sections.h2: What does Martin County list as its recording charges?
sections.html:
The county prints a fee sheet that mirrors state law and carries a warning that fees can change. Confirm the total with the office before mailing anything, and make money orders payable to the Martin County Register of Deeds.

Fee lines copied from the Martin County register of deeds page
ServiceCharge
Deed or other instrument, pages 1 to 15$26
Pages beyond 15$4 each
Deed of trust, pages 1 to 35$64
Plat or map (18 x 24)$21.00 a page
State right of way plans$21.00 first page, $5.00 after
Certified copy$5.00 first page, $2.00 after
Uncertified photocopy$0.25 a page
Deed excise tax$2.00 per $1000 of price
Cancellation or satisfactionNo fee
Extra instrument within one document$10.00 each

A re-recorded instrument costs the same as the original unless pages were added, and each added page is $4.

sections.h2: How should a deed be formatted before it goes to Martin County?
sections.html:
Instruments signed on or after July 1, 2002 must follow the layout rules the county quotes from G.S. 161-10, or the office adds a $25.00 nonstandard fee on top of the recording charge.

  • Paper size of 8 1/2 by 11 or 8 1/2 by 14 inches.
  • A 3-inch blank band across the top of the first page, and half-inch margins elsewhere.
  • Black ink on white paper, a font of at least 9 points, one side only.
  • The kind of instrument written at the top of page one.

Pen is acceptable for filling blanks and for corrections. Exhibits and attachments follow the same rules. The date that counts is the signing date, not the date the paper reaches the counter.

sections.h2: Which side pays the deed tax on a Martin County sale?
sections.html:
The seller does. The county's fee sheet shows the rate as $2.00 per $1000 of the purchase price, and state law words the same rate as $1.00 for each $500 or part of $500.

The register collects it at filing. One half stays in the county general fund and one half goes to the state, with a county retention of 2 percent of the state portion.

Your settlement statement prints the dollar figure. Do not estimate it in advance, since the office will not file the deed until it is paid.

sections.h2: Why does the order of filing matter in Williamston?
sections.html:
G.S. 47-18 makes registration the moment a conveyance, option, long lease or right of first refusal takes effect against lien creditors and paying purchasers. For land in Martin County that means registration with this office, even for an owner who lives elsewhere.

Suppose a creditor files a judgment before your buyer's deed reaches the counter. The buyer may end up behind it. Closing attorneys avoid that by filing right after funds are confirmed.

  • Send the signed deed and any lender release in one packet.
  • Include the fee and the excise tax.
  • Ask for the book and page number once the deed is recorded.

sections.h2: When does Martin County send tax bills, and when is interest charged?
sections.html:
Filing a deed does not clear a tax bill. The tax collector mails real and personal property bills in July or August, and tax is due September 1. Payment without interest is accepted through January 5, moving to the next business day when that date falls on a weekend or holiday.

Beginning January 6 a 2 percent penalty applies, and three-fourths of one percent interest builds each month afterward. State law has the collector advertise unpaid real estate tax in the local paper between March 1 and June 30, and the page notes an extra cost to the taxpayer for the notice.

The collector's office is at 305 East Main Street, Room 125, Williamston, open 8 AM to 5 PM Monday through Friday. The phone is 252-789-4360. Ask for a payoff figure before closing so the bill is paid out of your proceeds.

sections.h2: What does the Census Bureau say about Martin County housing?
sections.html:
Martin County had 21,601 residents in mid-2025, 2.0 percent fewer than the April 2020 estimates base, and 11,071 housing units. Owners occupy 66.8 percent of housing for 2020 to 2024, and the median owner-occupied home was valued at $109,700.

Median household income came to $48,578 in 2024 dollars, and 19.7 percent of residents are in poverty. The Census Bureau counted zero building permits for 2025. About 26.9 percent of residents are 65 or older.

Modest values and older houses make deferred repair a common reason a conventional buyer's lender balks. A cash buyer can take the house as-is and close once title is clear. Ask your attorney to run the land records first so any uncancelled deed of trust is released before the closing date.

faqs.q: Where in Williamston is the Martin County register of deeds?
faqs.a: On the first floor of the Martin County Governmental Building. The county page lists (252) 789-4320 for questions about records.

faqs.q: How old are the Martin County land records?
faqs.a: They go back to 1771. The county says deeds can be searched at martinrod.org, and that its index of recorded instruments begins that year.

faqs.q: What is the Martin County fee for a deed of trust?
faqs.a: $64 for the first 35 pages, then $4 for each additional page or fraction. A regular deed is $26 for 15 pages.

faqs.q: Does Martin County charge for recording a mortgage satisfaction?
faqs.a: No. The county lists cancellations, certificates of satisfaction and notices of satisfaction at no fee.

faqs.q: Who pays Martin County's deed excise tax?
faqs.a: The seller. The county prints the rate as $2.00 per $1000 of purchase price, and the office collects it before recording.
